subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should browser-origin Admin HTTP RPC requests be rejected by the Gateway origin policy in every auth mode, including explicit `gateway.auth.mode="none"`, while Origin-less host automation remains supported?
rationale: The route is intentionally usable by private host automation and explicit no-auth ingress, so the permanent browser-versus-host trust boundary must be confirmed before choosing origin enforcement, CSRF tokens, or a compatibility exception.

options.title: Enforce origin checks universally
options.body: Reject disallowed browser `Origin` values before Admin HTTP RPC dispatch in every auth mode while continuing to accept trusted Origin-less automation.

options.title: Limit checks to identity auth
options.body: Keep explicit no-auth ingress outside the browser-origin policy and document that operators must provide equivalent protection at their private ingress.

options.title: Require a CSRF token
options.body: Add a separate token requirement for browser-origin mutations, accepting the additional client and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Enforce origin checks universally
recommendation.body: Reject disallowed browser `Origin` values before Admin HTTP RPC dispatch in every auth mode while continuing to accept trusted Origin-less automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline explicitly routed the security-boundary question to this person, while implementation history is shared across plugin and Gateway contributors.
